messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info

message.content:
The largest planet that has been observed and confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 (about 320 light‑years away in the constellation Musca) and is still forming inside a protoplanetary disk.  Its radius is estimated to be roughly **2.5–3 times that of Jupiter**, making it the biggest planet we’ve ever measured.

> *Key facts*  
> • **Name:** HD 100546 b  
> • **Host star:** HD 100546 (A0V star)  
> • **Distance:** ~320 light‑years (≈98 parsecs)  
> • **Radius:** ≈ 2.5–3 R_Jupiter (≈ 180,000–220,000 km)  
> • **Mass:** Roughly 10–20 M_Jupiter (though the exact value is uncertain because it’s still accreting material).  

Because HD 100546 b is still accreting gas from its surrounding disk, its size and mass may change over time.  No other exoplanet has been found that exceeds this radius, so it holds the record for the largest known planet in the universe.
